name: Centro
etymology_summary: Self-explanatory: the historic centre of Madrid, the original core around the Puerta del Sol and Plaza Mayor.

name: Arganzuela
etymology_summary: From 'Arganduela' meaning 'Pequena Arganda' (little Arganda). Settlers from Arganda del Rey established themselves on the south bank of the Manzanares river.

name: Retiro
etymology_summary: From the Palacio del Buen Retiro (1633), built by Felipe IV as a royal retreat. The word 'retiro' means retreat/rest. Origin traces to the San Jeronimo el Real monastery where monarchs retired during Lent and mourning periods.

name: Salamanca
etymology_summary: Named after Jose de Salamanca y Mayol (1811-1883), Marquis of Salamanca, politician, financier, and real estate developer who planned and built the neighbourhood in the mid-19th century.

name: Chamartin
etymology_summary: Former independent municipality annexed in 1948. Etymology disputed and unclear. Possibly pre-Roman origin.

name: Tetuan
etymology_summary: Named 'Tetuan de las Victorias' after Spanish troops returning from victory at Tetouan (Morocco) in the African War of 1860. The soldiers camped in this area upon their return, and the settlement that grew around it took the name.

name: Chamberi
etymology_summary: Disputed etymology with multiple theories: (1) French regiment 'Chambery' during War of Independence; (2) Salesas nuns from Chambery, Savoy, connected to Queen Barbara de Braganza's convent; (3) Connection to Queen Luisa Gabriela de Saboya; (4) Possible Celtic origin. Most historians favour the Savoy/convent connection.

name: Fuencarral-El Pardo
etymology_summary: Compound name. Fuencarral: from 'Fuente del Carral' or similar, referring to a water source. El Pardo: from the brownish/dark ('pardo') colour of the landscape of the royal hunting estate, or from the Manzanares banks' appearance.

name: Moncloa-Aravaca
etymology_summary: Compound name. Moncloa: from the Palacio de la Moncloa (now the official residence of the Prime Minister). Aravaca: Celtic origin, per Caridad Arias (2004), from pre-Roman linguistic roots.

name: Latina
etymology_summary: Named after Beatriz Galindo 'La Latina' (1465-1534), a humanist scholar who was Latin tutor and advisor to Queen Isabel la Catolica. She founded the Hospital de la Latina in this area.

name: Carabanchel
etymology_summary: Disputed etymology with multiple theories: (1) Celtic origin; (2) 'Karavan' (caravans for commerce); (3) 'Garbanzal' (chickpea field); (4) Arabic 'Carab' (cultivable land, per Jaime Oliver Asin). Former independent municipalities (Alto and Bajo) annexed in 1948.

name: Usera
etymology_summary: Named after Marcelo de Usera, a 19th-century landowner who owned large estates in this area south of the Manzanares river.

name: Puente de Vallecas
etymology_summary: 'Vallecas' from 'Valle de Cas' (oak valley), documented as 'Balecas' in the 1202 Fuero de Madrid. 'Puente' (bridge) refers to a bridge over the Abroigal stream that connected the area to Madrid proper.

name: Moratalaz
etymology_summary: Possibly Arabic origin: from 'morata' (a type of blackberry/mulberry plant) combined with an Arabic suffix. Refers to the vegetation of the area.

name: Ciudad Lineal
etymology_summary: Named after Arturo Soria's revolutionary 1882/1886 'Ciudad Lineal' (linear city) urban planning concept -- a narrow city stretching along a single transportation axis. The boulevard Calle de Arturo Soria is its spine.

name: Hortaleza
etymology_summary: Disputed etymology: (1) Latin 'Orta Lucis' (sunrise, due to its eastern location); (2) Latin 'Hortus' (garden/orchards, referring to agricultural activity); (3) Corruption of 'Fortaleza' (fortress). Former independent municipality annexed in 1954.

name: Villaverde
etymology_summary: 'Villa verde' = green village/town, a descriptive name referring to the verdant landscape of this former independent municipality south of Madrid.

name: Villa de Vallecas
etymology_summary: See Puente de Vallecas for 'Vallecas' etymology (Valle de Cas = oak valley). 'Villa' denotes its former status as an independent municipality, in contrast to the part annexed earlier (Puente).

name: Vicalvaro
etymology_summary: From 'Vico Alvaro' = Alvaro's village/settlement. A pre-medieval personal name attached to the Latin 'vicus' (village). Former independent municipality annexed in 1951.

name: San Blas-Canillejas
etymology_summary: Compound name. San Blas: patron saint of the original parish church. Canillejas: ancient municipality documented from the 13th century, annexed in 1949. The etymology of Canillejas itself is uncertain.

name: Barajas
etymology_summary: Former independent municipality annexed in 1949. Possible Arabic origin from 'baraha' or similar root. Home to Madrid-Barajas airport. The exact etymology remains debated.
